questions: Should the function raise an error for invalid characters (non-parentheses, non-space) in the input string, or ignore them, or treat them as breaking the group?

If a group has mismatched parentheses (more closes than opens at any point), should the function raise an error, return a specific value (e.g., 0 or negative), or continue calculating max depth based on net depth?
Should empty groups (resulting from consecutive spaces) be ignored entirely, or should they produce a value (e.g., 0) in the output list?
Is the input guaranteed to have balanced parentheses within each group, or must the function handle unbalanced cases?
Should leading/trailing spaces in the input string be trimmed before processing, or treated as delimiting empty groups?
If a group is empty (e.g., due to multiple spaces), should it be skipped entirely or produce an output like 0?
Are there any constraints on the maximum depth or length of groups that the function should handle, or should it work for arbitrarily large inputs?
Should the function treat spaces as the only delimiter, or could other whitespace characters (tabs, newlines) also separate groups?
